The Tamil Nadu Artificial Intelligence

Mission (TNAIM) was established at the

Tamil Nadu e-Governance Agency (TNeGA) in

2024 for a period of two years to promote

research and innovation in Artificial Intelligence,

facilitate its adoption in governance and priority

sectors, undertake capacity-building initiatives

and ensure the ethical and responsible use of AI

technologies. The Government, in the Budget

Speech 2026-27 has announced the following:

“The Tamil Nadu Artificial Intelligence

Mission (TN AI Mission) will be

strengthened to encompass emerging

technologies such as Artificial Intelligence,

Quantum Technology, Animation, Visual

focus on AI applications in health,

agriculture, education, citizen services,

urban administration, social welfare

now function with the enhanced mandate of all

emerging technologies such as Artificial

Intelligence, Quantum Mission, AVGC-XR, deep

tech and other emerging technologies.

Every thread that passes through a weaver's

hands is not mere yarn; it is a work of art that

carries hard labour, livelihood, an artistic tradition

preserved across generations, and cultural pride.

The pleasant sound of the loom and the weaver's

delicate finger movements together transform

every piece of cloth into a cultural legacy.

Thiruvalluvar extols the greatness of this tireless

effort:

“அரு ருமை உமைத்த்தென் ன்று று அசாவாமை வவண் ண்டு டும்ம்

(திருக்குறள்–611)

The essence of this couplet is that greatness

comes only to those who act with unwavering

perseverance, without growing weary just because

a task is difficult. In the art of weaving, where skill

and patience go hand in hand, the dedication and

perseverance shown by generations of weavers

form the lifeblood of the handloom sector. Their

labour and artistic skill provide a firm foundation

for both the economic growth of Tamil society and

the preservation of its cultural heritage.

2

A continuing legacy for many centuries, this

sector not only preserves the traditional art of

weaving but also provides sustainable livelihoods

to lakhs of weavers and their families. In

particular, this sector makes a significant

contribution to the economic advancement and

social progress of women in rural and semi-urban

areas.

The origins of this distinguished tradition can

be traced back to the earliest Tamil literary

sources. Classical Sangam works such as the

Purananuru and Natrinai record the active

participation of women in weaving, highlighting

their contribution to household livelihoods. These

literary works portray weaving not merely as an

occupation but as an integral part of the cultural,

social and economic fabric of ancient Tamil society.

The Purananuru refers to garments woven

with such exquisite workmanship that they were

extremely fine and delicate, resembling the outer

3

skin of a snake and the thin inner membrane found

“ொம்ம்புபுரிரி யன் ன்ன வடி டிவி வின காம்ம்பிபின் ன்

கமைெடு டு தசாலி லியி யின் ன் இமையணி ணி வாரா”

(Purananuru,383)

This rich literary heritage is further

corroborated by archaeological evidence.

Excavations at Keeladi, Kodumanal, Uraiyur and

accessories and other artefacts, demonstrating the

advanced knowledge and technical expertise
